The approach addresses the specific challenges of indoor scenes, such as auto-exposure induced blur and sparse viewpoint coverage [S1].

The claim states that the approach addresses specific challenges of indoor scenes, namely auto-exposure induced blur and sparse viewpoint coverage. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly confirms both points: 1) It mentions that ScanNet videos are captured with auto-exposure held, leading to motion blur, and describes filtering out blurry images. 2) It notes that indoor scenes result in 'fewer images observing the same part of the space' (sparse viewpoint coverage) and describes how the method initializes the voxel grid using depth maps to handle this and reduce 'floaters' caused by sparse observations. Therefore, every fact in the claim is supported by the evidence.
